blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Rootstock block 9109008, DoCToken 0xe700691d owner() = MoCExchange 0x6acb83bb…; totalSupply ~2.99e6 DOC. Live DOC bytecode has burn(address,uint256) and owner() but no pause/blacklist/freeze selectors or strings. Verified OwnerBurnableToken burn is onlyOwner. MoCExchange uses that burn only inside redeem paths (redeemFreeDoc/doDocRedeem/redeemAllDoc). User-facing MoC (DeployableMoC) always calls mocExchange.redeemFreeDoc(msg.sender, …) and redeemAllDoc(msg.sender, msg.sender); connector.isWhitelisted(MoC 0xf773B590…) = true at the same block, so the only live whitelisted entry point binds burns to the redeeming user. Upgrade of MoCExchange remains a mint/governance risk (see mintAuthority), not a current freeze primitive. At Arbitrum block 489419615, DOC MyOFT 0x2ad62eb9 owner = 0xb2395eaa…; bytecode has owner/setPeer/transfer but no blacklist/pause/burn(address). Ethereum eDOC 0x69f6d4d4 is a bridge SideToken with minter = RSK Bridge and no blacklist/pause selectors. Failure domains: Rootstock MoC governance upgrade path; Arbitrum OFT owner; Ethereum RSK bridge multisig/federation — none is a live DOC transfer blacklist.
blacklistabilityReview.upstreamSuppressionRationale: rBTC collateral and LayerZero/RSK-bridge route risks can impair claim value or peripheral representation solvency, but they do not give those upstream actors a current holder-level freeze or blacklist on Rootstock DOC, Arbitrum DOC OFT, or eDOC transfer paths.

oracleRisk.summary: Money On Chain's pooled rBTC system consumes the OMoC BTC/USD feed, where up to ten staked operators use off-chain quorum signatures and elected fallback publishers. An April 2026 consensus-bypass flaw prompted a protocol panic pause; the protocol's incident report states the bug was fixed.

branchApplicability.rationale: Money On Chain documents one shared C0 bucket whose global rBTC coverage determines protocol states. DOC holders mint and redeem against the pooled system rather than opening borrower-specific debt positions, and the terminal liquidation state is a global, irreversible settlement that permits DOC redemption at the last available price. There are therefore no collateral-market liquidation branches to inventory.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: DOC is natively a Rootstock rBTC-collateralized CDP stablecoin. Its Arbitrum deployment (0x2ad62eb9...) is a self-deployed LayerZero V2 OFT representation documented by Money On Chain. Its low-supply Ethereum deployment is the legacy RSK Token Bridge eDOC SideToken (0x69f6d4d4...): at Ethereum block 25580192, the verified Bridge mapped original Rootstock token 0xe700691d... to eDOC in both directions. eDOC's sole minter was that Bridge proxy; upgrades and bridge ownership terminated at a 2-of-3 MultiSigWallet, while mint claims required the bridge's 2-of-5 Federation. Both peripheral deployments are external lock/mint routes rather than canonical rollup bridges.

routes.reviewNote: At Ethereum block 25580192, the verified Bridge's originalTokens(eDOC) returned Rootstock DOC 0xe700691d and mappedTokens(Rootstock DOC) returned eDOC, establishing the asset mapping on-chain. eDOC minter() returned Bridge proxy 0x12ed6935. The proxy implementation was 0x9f29f9bd and ProxyAdmin was 0xe4d35191; both ProxyAdmin.owner() and Bridge.owner() returned MultiSigWallet 0x040007b1 with required=2 and three owners. Bridge.getFederation() returned proxy 0x5e29c223, whose verified implementation required two votes from five enumerated members.
